t: Ancient sources put the Persian army at between 250,000 and 600,000 men, while most modern historians think it was no larger than 100,000 and Hans Delbrück gives as few as 25,000.
The battle was fought on a coastal plain only 2.6 km wide between the Gulf of Issus and the mountains, where Darius could not use his superiority in numbers.
It was the first time the Persian army had been defeated with the King present, and the battle has been called the beginning of the end of Persian power.
dyk: Where the Persian army was camped, the distance from the Gulf of Issus to the mountains is only 2.6 km, and the exact course of the Pinarus river there has been argued over for more than 80 years.
ev: Alexander crosses into Asia and defeats the Persian satraps at the Battle of the Granicus
Alexander occupies most of Asia Minor, taking coastal settlements such as Miletus and Halicarnassus
Darius marches north around the mountains, captures Issus and cuts Alexander's supply lines
Alexander's army defeats the Persians on the Pinarus and Darius flees
The Spartan king Agis III defeats the Macedonian general Coragus in the Peloponnese
Agis is finally defeated at the Battle of Megalopolis

f.place: South of the ancient city of Issus, near present-day Iskenderun in Turkey, on either side of a small river called the Pinarus; the identity of the river is disputed
f.sides: The Hellenic League under Alexander the Great, perhaps no more than 40,000 men including allies; the Achaemenid Empire under Darius III, whose army is put at no more than 100,000 by most modern historians, against 250,000 to 600,000 in ancient sources
f.outcome: The Macedonian and allied troops defeated the Persian forces. Darius fled, and Alexander captured his wife, daughters, mother and treasury.
